name: Image 2.5
description: Generate and edit images with OpenAI GPT Image 2.5 (or an OpenAI-compatible relay), with a masonry gallery you can re-edit from: text-to-image, image-to-image, masked edits, transparent backgrounds and custom sizes.
appView.description: Browse every image you generated, with the model, quality and size it was made with.
systemPrompt: Use image_gen_create to generate images with OpenAI's image API. Text-to-image: pass only prompt. Image-to-image / reference-guided editing: also pass reference_image_paths (local absolute file paths); add mask_path to limit the edit to a masked area. COST POLICY: unless the user explicitly asks for something better, keep the cheap defaults — model gpt-image-2.5-flare, quality low, size 1024x1024. Do not upgrade quality or resolution on your own initiative; quality goes low → medium → high → xhigh → max and both quality and size drive cost and waiting time. Only switch to gpt-image-2.5-sunburst when precise editing matters, and say why when you do. size takes 'auto' or WIDTHxHEIGHT (1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, 2048x2048, 2560x1440, 3840x2160 …). Set background='transparent' (with png or webp) when the user needs a cut-out. For a long, high-quality single render, pass partial_images 1-3 so progress stays visible. Generated images are saved locally as absolute file paths in the tool result and are also collected in the Image 2.5 gallery (left sidebar App View, or the Image 2.5 panel inside a session) — tell the user that when they ask where their pictures went; do not re-download or re-encode them, and use wechat_send or Session attach to show or share them. When the user attaches an image annotation or a boxed image region from that gallery, treat the attached file as the thing to edit: pass its path in reference_image_paths and apply the requested changes, honouring each box as the area to change. If the tool reports the OpenAI API key is missing, tell the user to open the Image 2.5 entry in Toolcase, click its settings (gear) menu and choose "OpenAI API Key" to paste it in. That settings menu also holds the "API Base URL" for a proxy/relay endpoint instead of api.openai.com. The Image 2.5 button in the Composer toolbar sets the everyday generation defaults instead: default model, default quality and default size (a single image_gen_create call can still override model/quality/size, or base_url for a one-off endpoint). When a request is blocked or rejected, the tool returns the API error code and a remediation hint — follow the hint instead of retrying the identical request.
tool.title: Generate Image
tool.description:
Generate an image with OpenAI's GPT Image API, or edit/remix one using reference images and an optional mask.
- Text-to-image: pass only "prompt".
- Image-to-image (reference-guided generation/editing): also pass "reference_image_paths" with one or more local absolute image file paths; add "mask_path" to restrict the edit to a masked area.
- size takes "auto" or WIDTHxHEIGHT: 1024x1024 (square), 1536x1024 (landscape), 1024x1536 (portrait), 2048x2048, 2048x1152, 2560x1440, 3840x2160. Custom sizes need multiples of 16, an aspect ratio within 3:1, edges ≤3840px.
- quality: low (fast drafts) → medium → high → xhigh → max. Unless the user asks for better, stay on the cheap defaults (flare + low + 1024x1024); higher quality and larger sizes cost more and take longer.
- background "transparent" (with output_format png/webp) gives a cut-out image; output_format png/jpeg/webp plus output_compression control the file.
- For a slow single render, partial_images 1-3 streams low-resolution previews so progress stays visible.
Generated images are saved to local files and collected in the Image 2.5 gallery (left sidebar App View, or the Image 2.5 panel in a session), where the user can preview them, draw boxes on one and send it back for another pass. When a gallery annotation or boxed region is attached to your message, pass that file in reference_image_paths and treat each box as the area to change. Use wechat_send or Session attach afterward to show/share the images — do not try to re-download or re-encode them yourself.
Requests go to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured in this mini tool's settings menu in Toolcase (default api.openai.com); pass base_url to override it for a single call only.
A failed call returns the API error code plus a remediation hint — change the prompt, size or inputs as instructed rather than retrying unchanged.

dialog.apiKey.desc: Paste your OpenAI API key. It is stored locally and only sent to the API endpoint used by Image 2.5 — never shown in chat.
dialog.model.desc: Used when a request does not name a model. Sunburst is tuned for editing precision, Flare for fast everyday generation.
dialog.quality.desc: Used when a request does not name a quality. auto lets the model decide; low is cheapest and fastest, max is the most detailed.
dialog.size.desc: Used when a request does not name a size. Either "auto" or WIDTHxHEIGHT (1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536 …) with edges that are multiples of 16. Default is {default}.
dialog.invalidSize.title: Invalid size
dialog.baseUrl.desc: OpenAI-compatible base URL, e.g. a proxy/relay endpoint. Leave empty to use the official {default}.
dialog.invalidUrl.title: Invalid URL
dialog.invalidUrl.message: "{value}" is not a valid http(s) URL. The base URL was not changed.
result.fromPartial: The endpoint streamed previews but no final image, so the last preview was saved — it may be lower resolution than requested.
error.noKey: OpenAI API key is not configured. Ask the user to open the Image 2.5 entry in Toolcase, click its settings (gear) menu → "OpenAI API Key" to enter it, then retry.
